blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: The required case study: the Orange River of southern Africa - the opportunities it presents, the hazards it brings, and how far they are managed.

blocks.heading: The Orange River: opportunities
blocks.text: The Orange is southern Africa's longest river. It rises as the Senqu in the mountains of Lesotho and flows westward about 2,200 kilometres across South Africa, forming the border with Namibia over its last stretch and entering the Atlantic at Alexander Bay; at Augrabies it plunges about 60 metres through a rocky gorge. Its lower valley is desert, with rainfall often under 100 millimetres a year, so the river's water is the opportunity that matters most. At Aussenkehr and Noordoewer on the Namibian stretch, irrigation schemes pump river water onto vineyards whose table grapes are exported abroad, and along the South African bank at Vioolsdrif the same water feeds smallholdings. Far upstream, the Gariep Dam, completed in 1971 and South Africa's largest reservoir, stores water for towns and farms and generates hydro-electric power.

blocks.heading: The hazard and its management
blocks.text: The Orange floods in the summer rainy season, when storms over its huge basin gather into a high pulse downstream. In 1988 one of the largest floods of the twentieth century on the river inundated camps and vineyards along the lower Orange, damaging the irrigation schemes around Kakamas and Aussenkehr and sweeping away pumps and piping. Management has partly succeeded since. The Gariep Dam (1971) and the Vanderkloof Dam (1977) upstream store and release water steadily, which lowers the flood peaks reaching the schemes, and embankment walls and rebuilt pump stations protect the irrigated land. Summer floods still interrupt farming, so the hazard is reduced rather than removed.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The Orange supplies topic 3.6's water supply with its southern African example, its flood plain and hazards belong with 2.2.1's processes, and its vineyards illustrate the export farming of topic 3.2. The river's map - source, border and mouth - is also practice for the skills of topic 4.
